subject: SLA action register & QBR OKR alignment
thread_summary: Postmortem of the 2027-02-09 throttling event converted into a consolidated SLA action register for QBR. Leadership asked for owners, timelines, and OKR alignment; external customer credit request noted. Final consolidated action register attached and owners assigned.
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-10T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Postmortem digest: 2027-02-09 throttling event

Team,

Attached is a short digest of the throttling incident on 2027-02-09 (attachment: postmortem-digest-20270209.pdf). Key points:
- Root cause: an unexpected traffic spike + suboptimal KV cache warmup for a new model routing policy.
- Impact: sustained 8–12s tail latencies for 20 minutes for a subset of hosted API customers; one customer (Acme Health) observed repeated timeouts.
- Immediate fixes deployed: throttling mitigation and routing rollback at 08:40 PST.

I started an action register (attached) with initial items; requesting leadership input on priority and which items must be in the QBR slide deck.

Initial action highlights (owners tentative):
1) Warmup strategy: implement pre-warm for model-variant pools (owner: Marcus) — ETA 2 weeks
2) Prefix KV cache persistence for hot keys (owner: Neha) — ETA 3 weeks
3) SLA credits / customer communication (owner: Laura) — ETA 3 days
4) Improved routing telemetry (owner: Rishi) — ETA 1 week

Please review the register and flag any missing actions.

Thanks,
Marissa
Principal SRE
Redwood Inference

Attachments: postmortem-digest-20270209.pdf

From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-10T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Postmortem digest: 2027-02-09 throttling event

Thanks Marissa — digest is clear. A couple of notes from GTM/CS side:
- Acme Health has requested a formal SLA credit and a short explanation they can share internally. I'll draft the credit proposal and the customer-facing summary.
- We should decide whether the incident requires a temporary change to the standard SLA language (e.g., expanded maintenance window/exception clause) before the QBR.

For the QBR slide: include the impact by revenue tier and then our remediation roadmap. I'll own customer comms + credit.

Laura
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-10T11:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Postmortem digest: 2027-02-09 throttling event

Adding metric context and a concrete owner split. Metric notes:
- Peak QPS on impacted pool: 1.9x baseline (09:07–09:12 PST)
- 95th pct latency delta: +6s; 99.9th pct delta: +11s for affected shards

Action edits:
- Warmup strategy (Marcus) — break into: a) pre-warm policy (1 week experimental), b) autoscale thresholds (2 weeks), c) runbook update (3 days).
- KV cache persistence (Neha) — propose checkpointing hot keys to local NVMe on drain.
- Routing telemetry (Rishi) — add synthetic traffic test for peak patterns.

I'll update the register and push a draft of the slide that shows the timeline + mitigations.

Marcus
Director, Platform Reliability

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-11T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Postmortem digest: 2027-02-09 throttling event

Team — thanks for the quick turnaround. Two leadership asks before the QBR prep loop:
1) Convert the action register into a single page "SLA action register" with: owner, ETA, risk (low/med/high), OKR mapping (which Q1/Q2 OKR this supports), and customer impact. This is what we'll circulate with the exec readout.
2) For any action that changes SLA language or entitlements, include legal/procurement impact notes and attach the proposed wording.

Laura: please include the customer credit draft by EOD Thursday. Marcus/Neha: prioritize items that materially reduce tail latency for hosted customers (we'll mark as high risk/priority).

I'll review the consolidated register on Friday and finalize what goes to the QBR.

Vivek
Head of Product Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Acme Health <support@acmehealth.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-12T09:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Incident impact on Acme Health — request for credit

Laura,

Thanks for the update. The timeouts caused our nightly ingestion job to fail and required manual reprocessing (approx. 4 engineer-hours). We appreciate Redwood's quick remediation. Please confirm the scope of any credit and an ETA for the warmup fix — our compliance team will want a date to track.

Regards,
Samir Patel
SRE Lead, Acme Health

Attaching the consolidated SLA action register (Redwood_SLA_Action_Register_20270214.xlsx). Summary of changes:
- Owners confirmed, ETAs revised after engineering review.
- Risk column added, OKR mapping column added (Q1-Reliability; Q2-Scale Ops).
- New item: synthetic peak-pattern test runner (owner: Rishi) — ETA 10 days (high risk).

Quick excerpt (from sheet):
- Item: Pre-warm policy for model-variant pools | Owner: Marcus | ETA: 2027-02-21 | Risk: High | OKR: Q1-Reliability
- Item: KV cache checkpointing | Owner: Neha | ETA: 2027-03-03 | Risk: Medium | OKR: Q2-Scale Ops
- Item: Customer credit proposal | Owner: Laura | ETA: 2027-02-14 | Risk: Low | OKR: Q1-Customer Trust

Next steps: Vivek to review and mark final list for QBR slide. Laura to confirm credit wording; Marcus/Neha to confirm delivery timelines in next standup.

Neha
Staff Engineer, Platform

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-02-14T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Finalize: SLA action register & QBR inclusion

Marked final after review — thank you all. A few final notes before I close the loop:
- Laura: proceed with the credit; include one-line public-safe summary for the QBR slide.
- Marcus: prioritize the pre-warm policy experiment; if metrics show positive signal, prepare a short demo for the QBR (1 slide).
- Neha: include a short risk mitigation note on persistence approach and potential perf impact.
- Rishi (cc'd on the register): ensure telemetry feeds into the synthetic test runner so we can show pre/post graphs in the QBR.

I've uploaded the final register to the doc link in related_links and attached the spreadsheet to this thread. We'll include the single-page SLA action register in the QBR packet under the reliability chapter.

Vivek
Head of Product Ops
Redwood Inference
